source.title: Deep Learning is Provably Robust to Symmetric Label Noise
source.authors: Carey E. Priebe; N. Huang; Soledad Villar; Cong Mu; Li Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study derives an asymptotic result for symmetric label noise and reports CNN simulations on noisy image datasets; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiments.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports test classification performance across symmetric label-noise probabilities. The paper does not report training error for these experiments, so the figure cannot establish that the networks fit the noisy training labels perfectly. Referenced findings from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The simulations and original theoretical result bear on V4's test-error response to random label corruption. They do not test perfect fitting of noisy training labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish asymptotic Bayes optimality for L1-consistent DNN classifiers under symmetric label noise below (K-1)/K without noise mitigation, and describe their simulations as supporting the threshold. They do not establish that these simulations perfectly fit noisy training labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes symmetric label noise and clean-test performance rather than fitting completely random labels and measuring both training and test error. Its numerical simulations train CNNs on noisy MNIST and CIFAR10.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and symmetric label-noise probability are varied; the paper states that performance degrades very slowly until the statistical limit.
record.problems: The reported numerical evidence is presented in figures without values in the text; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The experiments do not report training error, so they cannot show perfect fitting of the noisy labels.
record.rows_left_out: No symmetric-noise results were left out. Figure 2 reports class-dependent noise, which is outside the claim versions' specified symmetric or random-label conditions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed across corruption levels.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout the corruption sweep, memorization of corrupted examples, and empirical chance performance at completely random labeling.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noise.

missing.what: An original theoretical result establishes that L1-consistent DNN classifiers attain clean Bayes risk asymptotically for every symmetric noise probability below (K-1)/K. It qualifies increasing test error under corruption, without establishing training interpolation.

record.verdict_notes: Slow empirical degradation alone does not contradict steady degradation. The supplied text cannot establish numerical trajectories or uncertainty. For ten classes, alpha=0.9 produces labels independent of the true class; alpha=1 always excludes the true class and is not completely random labeling.

versions.untested_parts: Random labeling of the training set, training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters are not tested.
Training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases are not reported.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
The paper reports clean-test performance across symmetric label-noise levels but does not report training error, so perfect training fit and the full joint claim are not established.
The study does not compare weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation, nor test their removal.
The study does not report training-time ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with symmetric label noise and evaluated on the original clean test dataset.
rows.measure: Classification performance on the original test dataset
rows.note: The text says performance degrades very slowly until the statistical limit, but does not give plotted values or training error. The architecture has two convolution layers followed by two fully connected layers; training used SGD, batch size 64, learning rate 0.01, 3 epochs, and momentum 0.5.
rows.check: The text reports very slow degradation, but the supplied figure contains no readable values. Neither the full test-error trajectory nor training fit can be established. Noise probability alpha denotes flipping to a different class: labels become completely uninformative at alpha=0.9, not alpha=1.
